Industries we serve

Robots for the work that's hardest to staff.

We rent commercial robots to the operations that need them most — warehouses, hospitals, hotels, facilities. We own, install, service, and back every unit.

Get a free site assessment

Service Robot Co. rents commercial robots to the operations where the work is most repetitive, physical, and hard to staff — warehouses, hospitals, hotels, restaurants, property management, builders, facilities, law enforcement, and more. We own the robot, the deployment, the maintenance, and the downtime. You pay one monthly or per-job fee and get a working machine on site. Every rental includes setup, ongoing service, and a backup unit, backed by Regional service engineers and depots in all 50 states.

More industries we serve

Same rental model. Different settings, different robots.

Law enforcement & public safety

Put a camera under a vehicle, into a building, or down a void — without putting an officer there first.

Government procurement moves on its own timeline and through its own channels. For law enforcement and public-safety teams, the primary use case we see is situational awareness — putting eyes on a perimeter, a vehicle undercarriage, or a structure entry point before a person has to go near it. The question is not whether a robot is useful; it is finding one that has already cleared the procurement and certification hurdles your agency requires.

See robots for Law enforcement →

Property management

Keep common areas clean across a portfolio of buildings.

The two use cases that come up most often for property managers are overnight floor cleaning in lobbies and common corridors, and delivery robots for amenity runs — packages, dry cleaning, or food orders moving from the front desk or a receiving room up to residents. In both cases the economics work because the robot covers a route the building runs every day, and the rental model means you are not holding hardware in a building where the work is light.

See robots for Property management →

Builders & GCs

Automate the repetitive, physical work on a job site — floor care on large slabs and material movement.

The two most common robot deployments on construction sites are scrubbers on large concrete slabs and camera trailers for outdoor site security. Floor scrubbers go in when a building is at the point where a hard floor exists and needs to be kept clean — during interior finishing or post-construction handoff prep. The math works because a robot covers ground overnight that would otherwise take multiple crew members hours, without the safety exposure of night-shift cleaning on an active site.

See robots for Builders & GCs →

Facilities

Keep large floors clean across a building or campus.

Large floor plans are the defining constraint in facilities work. A single scrubber covers ground at a consistent pace, on the same schedule, every night — without fatigue, without call-outs, and without the coordination overhead of a cleaning crew working a multi-building campus. The Gausium Scrubber 75 is the unit we see most in facilities deployments: it is sized for large open floor plates, quiet enough to run in occupied spaces, and reliable enough to run unattended.

See robots for Facilities →

Parking Lots & Vehicle Lots

Eyes on every row all night — camera trailers and patrol robots stop theft before it starts.

Open lots are a theft target the moment they go dark. Catalytic-converter theft, break-ins, and vandalism all spike in the hours after close, when one guard walking the perimeter cannot see every row at once and the cost of that guard often exceeds the lot's nightly revenue. A mobile camera trailer changes the math: 30-ft mast, up to nine cameras, 360° coverage, loudspeaker and strobe deterrents — and it brings its own power and cellular connection, so there is no wait on utilities, no permitting, no trenching.

See robots for Parking lots →

Malls & Shopping Centers

Keep concourses, food courts, and retail corridors spotless — day and night, without adding cleaning staff.

The defining challenge in malls is floor area that never fully stops seeing foot traffic. A food court that runs from 10am to 10pm leaves a narrow overnight window for cleaning, and a crew large enough to cover 50,000 sq ft in that window is expensive to staff consistently. An autonomous scrubber runs the same route every night on a schedule the property sets — same quality, zero call-outs, no coordination overhead.

See robots for Malls →

Schools & Higher Education

Cover campus delivery, cleaning, and patrol without hiring for every shift.

See robots for Schools & Higher Ed →

Event Venues & Stadiums

Scaled-up security coverage for a window of days — without scaling headcount.

Event days multiply the footprint of a venue: overflow parking in a field, a temporary entrance gate on the far side of the lot, vendor areas that did not exist yesterday. A permanent camera system does not cover temporary ground, and hiring additional guards for a one-day window is expensive and logistically difficult. Mobile camera trailers cover the temporary or overflow areas, deter and document, and leave when the event is over.

See robots for Event venues →

Common questions

Which industries do you serve?
Service Robot Co. rents and runs commercial robots for warehouses and 3PL, hospitals and healthcare, hotels and hospitality, restaurants, parking lots and vehicle lots, event venues and stadiums, property management, builders and GCs, facilities, law enforcement, and more. The same rental model applies across all of them — we own the robot, the deployment, the service, and the backup.
Do you serve parking lots and outdoor sites?
Yes. Mobile camera trailers and patrol robots are the primary solution for parking lots, open vehicle lots, and event venues. They are solar-powered, run on cellular, and deploy in under 30 minutes with no power or internet on site. Cleaning robots cover large surface lots and decks. We service both nationwide.
What robots does Service Robot Co. rent for commercial use?
The lineup includes autonomous mobile robots for warehouse material movement, delivery and serving robots for hospitality and healthcare, autonomous floor scrubbers for cleaning, mobile camera trailers and patrol robots for security, and cobots for manufacturing. Each industry gets the robot that fits its real operational need.
Do you service nationwide across all industries?
Yes. Every rental includes deployment, setup, ongoing maintenance, and a backup unit — backed by Regional service engineers and depots in all 50 states. 24/7 emergency response, 24-hour nationwide on-site dispatch, and 10-minute remote triage during business hours.
Can I rent robots for a specific industry without a long contract?
Yes. Rentals run per job or month-to-month. You scale up for the work in front of you and scale back after — we do not lock you into a fleet you cannot use.
